subject: Recap: CardinalPay call — cost levers, success criteria & pilot scope
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lee <kate@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: CardinalPay call — cost levers, success criteria & pilot scope

Hi Kate — thanks for the call today. Quick recap so we’re aligned and so Monica/Karthik have the context for next steps.

Pain points you shared:
- Per-transaction token costs are eating margin on realtime scoring (esp. dispute/KYC flows).
- Latency spikes during peak hours cause user-visible retries and increased infra spend.
- Current provider offers limited control over batching/caching and no private deployment option.

Current stack you described:
- Production: OpenAI API for generation + in-house microservice that fans out scoring across several models (one call per candidate).
- Mix of short prompts (70%, <50 tokens) and long document summarization (30%, up to ~1k tokens).
- Some async workflows could be batched, but most realtime paths are single-request synchronous.

Primary success criteria for a pilot (what you want to measure):
1) Unit cost reduction target: 3x reduction in per-transaction inference cost (tokens-adjusted).
2) Latency SLO: 95th percentile < 250ms for realtime scoring routes.
3) Fidelity: <2% drop on your KYC/regression eval set if we apply quantization.
4) Operational readiness: evidence of SOC 2 + ability to run in a private or dedicated environment.

What we propose for the initial pilot (scope):
- Run a 2-week A/B pilot against a representative subset of realtime traffic (10–20k requests/day).
- Test quantized model variant (4-bit) on the scoring path + prefix KV caching for repeated prompts.
- Measure token/unit cost, latency percentiles, and fidelity on your gold prompts.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Kate: share a 500–1k prompt sample and the evaluation script (anonymized) — example template attached (example-prompt-set.csv).
- CardinalPay: confirm procurement/security contact for SOC 2 and encryption-at-rest questions.
- Redwood: we’ll draft a pilot charter and a preliminary cost estimate (attached: cardinalpay-poc-charter.pdf).
- Proposed kickoff week: Jun 7 (flexible).

Attachments referenced: cardinalpay-poc-charter.pdf (pilot scope), example-prompt-set.csv (sample prompt template).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short statement of work and a DocuSign link once we have the prompt sample.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192



From: Kate Lee <kate@cardinalpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@cardinalpay.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: CardinalPay call — cost levers, success criteria & pilot scope

Jordan & team — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few details from our side: 

1) Current environment: we’re on the OpenAI commercial API today. The breakdown you used is accurate (majority short, significant long tail for document summaries). The realtime scoring path is stateless and fans out to score ~4–6 candidates per request; that fanout is the main cost driver.

2) Batching/caching opportunities: we do have an async fraud queue (good candidate for batching). For realtime scoring, we can add a small cache at the microservice level (keyed by normalized user+prompt) — reasonable to get ~15–20% hit rate after warmup.

3) Quantization openness: engineering is willing to test quantized weights if you can show fidelity numbers on our eval set. KYC precision/recall is the non-negotiable metric.

4) Security/procurement: procurement will need SOC 2 Type II and an encryption-at-rest statement; I’ve looped them in. They’ll expect a security packet before we sign any PII-accessing pilot.

Kickoff timeline: Jun 8–11 works better for engineering (we have a release window earlier in June). Can you confirm availability?

Action: I’ll send the anonymized prompt sample and evaluation script by EOD tomorrow. Procurement will follow up with the SOC2 checklist.

— Kate
Kate Lee
Head of Product, CardinalPay
kate@cardinalpay.com


(attachment: cardinalpay-soc2-request.docx)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kate Lee <kate@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-23T09:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: CardinalPay call — cost levers, success criteria & pilot scope

Thanks Kate — appreciate the detail and the procurement loop. Quick replies inline + proposed plan: 

- Kickoff: we’re available Jun 8 and can reserve a small engineering kickoff slot. I’ll block time pending your confirmation.
- Pilot configuration (initial suggestion): Redwood Dedicated reserved pool + 4-bit quantized variant for scoring path; non-quantized for the long-document summarization route. Use prefix/KV cache on scoring route (expect ~15–20% hit rate based on your note).

Preliminary savings estimate (back-of-envelope):
- Quantized 4-bit + caching + reduced fanout (combine top-1 rerank instead of 4-candidate full calls) could get you ~2.5–3.5x reduction in per-transaction inference cost on the scoring route. We’ll validate in pilot.

Security/Procurement: we’ll assemble a security packet (SOC2 report, encryption statements, data handling playbook) and share via secure link.

Next steps I’ll action this week:
1) Finalize pilot charter and send DocuSign (link to follow).
2) Ask engineering for a short runbook for the Dedicated pilot (ops checklist, SLOs).
3) Schedule Jun 8 kickoff — please confirm availability.

Links: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/CRD-2027-045 | DocuSign (draft SOW): https://docusign.com/abc123

Thanks — will be in touch after I pull the security packet together.

— Jordan

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-24T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Recap: CardinalPay call — cost levers, success criteria & pilot scope

Monica / Karthik — forwarding the thread from CardinalPay with the asks. Short internal checklist for preparation: 

1) Pricing: draft a two-week pilot quote for a Dedicated reserved pool + burst capacity. Include a line for SRE support and quantization evaluation hours.
2) Ops runbook: Karthik, can you prepare a short checklist (service attach, KV cache configuration, expected metrics to collect: tokens, 95p latency, QPS).
3) Security packet: Monica, please prepare SOC2 excerpt + encryption-at-rest statement and data handling playbook for the pilot. Procurement will request these before signing.
4) Fidelity eval: we’ll need a script to run our quantized model against their eval set and produce precision/recall delta; attach to the pilot charter.

Target: have pricing + ops checklist + security packet ready by May 27 so Jordan can send DocuSign and lock Jun 8 kickoff if CardinalPay confirms.

Quoted from Kate’s email: 
> For realtime scoring, we can add a small cache at the microservice level (keyed by normalized user+prompt) — reasonable to get ~15–20% hit rate after warmup.

Atts: cardinalpay-poc-charter.pdf, example-prompt-set.csv, cardinalpay-soc2-request.docx

— Jordan
